title: What this costs
tagline: What it costs to run roofbeam.net, itemised from the actual expense tracker — including what is deliberately not counted, and what is still unknown.
card_question: What does it actually cost to keep the lights on here?
source: Roofbeam LLC 2026 expense tracker · figures as recorded, never estimated
tracker_note: The expense tracker is a tax record — it counts every deductible business expense. This page counts only upkeep: what recurs to keep the site and the toys running. The two totals below add back to the tracker's, so nothing is hidden by the split.
scope: This page covers roofbeam.net — the site and the toys on it. It does not cover onderdak.org ($23.99/yr), which Roofbeam bills for but which is a different project.

upkeep.what: Static hosting — serves the site and every toy
upkeep.note: Free tier. This is why the number below is small.
Registered 2026-07-29 through 2029-07-29 — about $19/yr spread across the three years.

upkeep.what: Cloud servers — the backend the toys will run on
upkeep.note: Two charges: $15.29 in May, $34.59 in June. Nothing since. The monthly rate is not established yet.
A single charge in February. Whether it recurs is not established.
The mailbox demonstrably exists — the domain publishes a Google DKIM key and routes mail to Google. What it costs has never been written down.

excluded.why: Unconfirmed. roofbeam.net runs on GitHub Pages, which is free — so this is most likely a personal blog, not this site. It is the largest line in the tracker and it is not counted here until that is settled.
Dictation software — a tool for doing the writing, not upkeep of the site.
Two hardware security keys. One-time, and hardware rather than upkeep.
The LLC formation filing. One-time, and it is the cost of the entity, not of the workshop.
Reference manager — a tool for the research, not upkeep of the site.

not_this_entity.why: Belongs to a previous LLC of the same name that was allowed to lapse. It is a different entity and its costs are not this workshop's. It is listed here because the record is confusing and the confusion should be public rather than private.
